cells.tense: You are the one keeping the blend right as it moves.
cells.act: care for it with fresh hands and see what it needs
cells.ask: Tend a thing you're running with fresh hands: look at it closely, adjust only what plainly asks for it, and leave the rest alone.
cells.core:
You're good at this. The mix is live — heat rising, someone needing more, the timing shifting — and you keep adjusting without making a fuss. You add when it's thin, take away when it's crowded, and the thing keeps moving because of it. Nothing is stuck. You can feel the day's shape before it arrives, and you're already tilting toward what it needs.

The balance holds because you keep showing up to it, not because it stays put. That's worth protecting. Tend a thing you're running the way you'd tend something young: eyes on it closely, only what it asks for, nothing forced. You'll learn its actual rhythm instead of the one you assumed it had, and you'll find which of your adjustments it didn't need.
cells.sheetLine: The blend stays right because you keep touching it.
cells.verb: hold steady while the mix keeps correcting

cells.tense: You are already in next week, correcting a mix that hasn't happened yet.
cells.act: put the inquiry on paper and follow it
cells.ask: Put one live question on paper — what actually happened, in order — and follow the page until the facts run out and the forecasting starts.
cells.core:
The correction has run past the present. You're adjusting for things that haven't happened — the shortfall next month, the way it'll go wrong, what you'll have to fix — and the mix at hand keeps getting solved for a version of itself that isn't here. So you work hard and it doesn't settle, because you're tuning a sound nobody has made yet. The energy is real. It's just spent before the moment it belongs to.

Set down what actually happened: what came in, what you did, what came out. In order. Plain words. Leave out how it felt and what you feared, and follow the page until it runs out of facts and into guesswork. You'll see where the record stops and the forecast begins, usually sooner than you expect, and often with less wrong than the bracing assumed.

cells.tense: You stopped adjusting, and the mixing keeps happening without you.
cells.act: lay the one step you can see, solidly
cells.ask: Lay one step you can already see, solidly — a shelf hung, a bill sent, a draft finished — so a single thing holds when you're done.
cells.core:
You're behind the moment you're in. The mix is moving — it does that — and you're not adjusting it anymore; you're standing beside it. Something ended and instead of the next step there was stillness, and the stillness held. You still see what needs doing. You just don't move toward it, and the days pass through the room without you in them.

One thing, laid solidly. Not the whole system — a step you can already see, done so it holds. A shelf that stays up. A bill sent. A route walked. Something physical and small and finished, so the day has one thing in it shaped by your hands. Strength comes back through what gets built, not through deciding to feel stronger. Put the stone down where you can see it.
cells.sheetLine: One solid step does more than any plan for the whole.

cells.tense: You are already steering this thing and calling it the situation.
cells.act: learn how it grows by tending it
cells.ask: Notice the next small adjustment you make to keep something moving, and name it quietly as your own doing. Then carry on.
cells.core:
The adjustments are happening and they don't have your name on them. You notice the room going flat and you change the temperature. Something's about to run short and you cover it before anyone asks. You'd say that's just how things go, or that anyone would have. The steering is constant and it's yours. The doing doesn't get counted, so it doesn't add up to anything you can hold.

Try catching one. The next time you make a small adjustment to keep something moving — the temperature, the timing, the thing nobody asked about — notice it as it happens and name it quietly as your own doing. No announcement, no credit, no explanation. Then carry on. Small honest noticing is how a thing gets its author back; the hands have been doing it without the name.
